topic: Non-Equivalence of Euclidean Distance and Dot Product Preference in Latent Space
problem_statement: Demonstrate whether nearest neighbor search via Euclidean distance in latent space is mathematically equivalent to Top-N recommendation ranking by ALS dot product.
solution_or_decision: Constructed mathematical counterexample where Item 1 is Euclidean-close to User (distance 0.1414, dot product 4.20) while Item 2 is Euclidean-far (distance 3.0000, dot product 10.00). ALS recommendation rank depends strictly on dot product p_u^T q_i which scales with factor norms, not Euclidean distance. Fast Top-N retrieval requires Maximum Inner Product Search (MIPS), not standard Euclidean k-d trees.
evidence: Counterexample verified: dist1 (0.1414) < dist2 (3.0000), yet dot2 (10.00) > dot1 (4.20).
